info.name: OAN — Network of Networks
info.description:
Two OAN networks side by side, each with its own registry, discovery and adapter.

**The demo, in order:**
1. Bharat 1 — publish mandi into A
2. Bharat 2 — search A, returns mandi only
3. Maha 1 — publish weather into B
4. wait ~30s, no manual crawl
5. Bharat 2 again — now returns mandi AND weather
6. Bharat 3 — select mandi, answered locally
7. Bharat 4 — select weather, crosses to B

Bring the stack up with `make network NETWORK_ID=...` in helmcharts/networkofnetwork. Full runbook in demo/README.md.

item.name: Bharat  (network A — has mandi)
item.description:
Network A. Publishes its OWN mandi catalogue, and crawls B every 30s so B's weather also answers here.

Ports: adapter 9300, discovery 9301.

request.description: A's own catalogue. visibleTo names ONLY A: there is no reason for another network to mirror it, and leaving B out is what stops B crawling it back.
No context.networkId. An omitted audience means no audience filter at all, so this returns everything A holds -- its own mandi AND the weather it crawled from B. The farmer never names a network.
context.receiverId is A, so A answers it from its own provider. Returns on_select with real prices from the mock.

SAME endpoint as 3. The only difference is context.receiverId, which the consumer copied out of the catalog: it names B, so A signs as itself and sends it to context.bppUri. The answer comes from B's provider.
Not needed for the demo -- A crawls every 30s on its own. Use it only to skip the wait. Takes no body: the crawler reads who to crawl from its registry.

item.name: Maha  (network B — has weather)
item.description:
Network B. Publishes its OWN weather catalogue and shares it with A.

B does NOT crawl: FEDERATION_CRAWL_PEERS=off. Otherwise each network mirrors the other and B ends up re-importing its own catalogue through A's copy of it.

Ports: adapter 9400, discovery 9401.

request.description: THE IMPORTANT FIELD IS visibleTo. It names A as well as B, which is the whole permission for A to mirror this. Drop A from it and A's crawl returns nothing -- no error, just nothing.
B holds only its own weather. Run it after A has crawled to show B did NOT import A's mandi back.
The same select as Bharat's #4, but sent straight to B. Same answer -- which is the point: A adds no special handling, it just forwards.
